answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-stake identity bonding: to join an agent economy, each account must lock collateral that is scarce and slashable, so every sybil name costs real capital. Like a voyage that plans its route around a ridge instead of pretending the terrain is flat, a well-designed market treats identity cost as terrain to design around rather than an obstacle to cheat. A zephyr is free, but identities are not: when influence is weighted by bonded stake per unique key and misbehavior burns the deposit, spawning thousands of clones yields zero extra power, only added cost.
